parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national layer governs entry and custody. A cable refuses applicants on any document or sex-evidence discrepancy, with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding. Passports have been confiscated or blocked, stranding some travellers. Immigration custody has documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans men. The state layer is strong: anti-discrimination law, a constitutional clause, corrected documents without surgery, insurer coverage and a correctional protection law. Its facilities rule is not documented here. The July 2026 assessment flags shortfalls in care equity and in incarcerated trans protections, and no state-level violence pattern is documented. Documented national exposure at entry and in custody outweighs the state's protections, placing the case in the Elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: Cable directs refusal on any document discrepancy or doubt about sex; possible permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked; X markers no longer issued.
entry_documents.protection: Documented: none operative for visitors at entry; the state's X marker applies only to state IDs, not foreign entry.
entry_documents.interaction: National entry screening applies regardless of state law; a mismatch can lead to refusal before any state protection is reached.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. National corrections policy from 2026 imposes conversion-style treatment and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State correctional protection law (2023) exists on paper; the July 2026 assessment finds it short in operation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A traveller detained at the border falls under federal custody, which the state statute does not reach.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National facility rules bar gender-identity access in federally funded single-sex facilities. The state's facilities map entry is not reproduced, so state facility access is unresolved; one state trespass-arrest report is not attributed to this state.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented: state anti-discrimination law covers public accommodation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules and state accommodation law may conflict; the dossier does not show which governs in practice.

care_services.exposure: Federal subpoenas for under-19 hospital records; proposed federal rules to bar public reimbursement for minors; national crisis-line LGBTQ youth services shut down.
care_services.protection: State law mandates insurer and public-programme coverage of gender-affirming care from January 2024; state health-equity shortfall documented qualitatively.
care_services.interaction: A visitor's state coverage may not reach a traveller with out-of-state insurance; federal record demands can reach state providers.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders direct investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a target category.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism statement disclaims targeting people who merely disagree; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat-framing is operative and sits above state protections; state police conduct toward visitors is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor visitors face federal care-record demands and possible proposed reimbursement bars; guardians with mismatched documents face the same entry refusal.
minors_guardians.protection: State care coverage and school anti-bullying law exist; minors' visiting exposure is not specifically documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's documents and a guardian's documents both go through national entry screening, so a family can be refused together.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-level incident of violence against trans people is documented; no state pattern can be described.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented: state hate-crime law covering gender identity, a hate-crime hotline (2025), and a constitutional equal-protection clause.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hate-crime recourse is state-level and operative in principle; the national frame does not contradict it here.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal passport suit unresolved; traveller exposure depends on which measures are in effect at travel; national custody remedies not shown to work.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State ombuds and anti-discrimination enforcement exist; the national legal-aid FAQ is informational only.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State recourse does not reach federal entry or custody decisions; oversight findings recur without visible correction.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has routine exclusion of visibly trans visitors with no effective appeal. Here the entry exposure is comparable for discrepant documents, but appeals and state recourse exist, and there is no universal exclusion of trans visitors. This case is higher.

0.55-B has secondary screening, admin refusal and humiliation, with a note that the penalty stays administrative. Here the federal custody record includes forced labour and sexual abuse, which is more severe. Lifetime fraud findings are possible. This case is lower, though state protections are stronger than 0.55-B's.

0.75-C has documented respectful border inspection and brief detention with remedies. Here the national entry cable and documented custody abuse are materially worse, and the state's protections do not reach federal decisions. This case is much lower.

parsed.synthesis: The state's strong protections (anti-discrimination, corrected documents, insurer and custody statutes) do not reach the national entry and custody exposures the dossier documents. A traveller with a document discrepancy meets refusal and possible permanent ineligibility at entry; a detained traveller meets documented federal custody harm, which state law does not govern. Federal care-record demands and threat framing add exposure that state care coverage does not cancel. The state's facility rule and violence record are undocumented, so they are not counted as exposure or protection. The combined regime therefore sits in the Elevated band, with the state's operative recourse acting as a partial mitigator only.
